plan: With a private value of $28, I want to maximize potential profit. Since values are randomly drawn between $0-$49, other bidders have similar incentives. A pure dominant strategy is challenging. I'll aim to bid slightly above my value but not excessively, anticipating rational behavior from others. A bid around $30-$35 seems strategic - high enough to potentially win, but not so high that I risk significant losses if my value is relatively low.

In a second-price sealed bid auction with values between $0-$49, the optimal strategy is to bid close to my true value. Since my value is $23, I want to bid strategically. Other rational bidders will likely bid near their own values. I'll bid slightly above my true value to increase my chances of winning, but not so high that I risk negative earnings. A bid around $25-$26 seems reasonable to account for potential competitive bidding.

In a single-round second-price sealed bid auction with values between $0-$49, the optimal strategy is to bid close to my true value. Since my private value is $36, I'll bid strategically. Other rational bidders will likely bid near their own values. I'll bid slightly below my true value to create a buffer - this protects against overpaying if their values are high. A bid around $34-$35 seems optimal, balancing potential win probability with profit protection.
